lessonTitle: 1. The power function with a natural exponent
lessonTitleEnglish: The power function with a natural exponent
unit: Algebra · Chapter 1. Power and exponential functions
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 11 mathematics textbooks (advanced stream)

stages.headline: f(x) = xⁿ (n ∈ ℕ) is the power function with a natural exponent; it is even for even n and odd for odd n.
stages.headlineEnglish: f(x) = xⁿ (n ∈ ℕ) is the power function with a natural exponent; it is even for even n and odd for odd n.

stages.headline: Even n: range [0; +∞), decreasing on (−∞; 0] and increasing on [0; +∞). Odd n: range ℝ, increasing on all of ℝ.
stages.headlineEnglish: Even n: range [0; +∞), decreasing on (−∞; 0] and increasing on [0; +∞). Odd n: range ℝ, increasing on all of ℝ.

stages.headline: For 0 < x < 1 the powers xⁿ decrease as n grows, for x > 1 they increase: 0.5² > 0.5³ but 2² < 2³.
stages.headlineEnglish: For 0 < x < 1 the powers xⁿ decrease as n grows, for x > 1 they increase: 0.5² > 0.5³ but 2² < 2³.

stages.headline: Find the range of f(x) = x⁴.
stages.headlineEnglish: Find the range of f(x) = x⁴.
stages.problemText: Find the range of f(x) = x⁴.
stages.solutionSteps: 1. Even exponent: x⁴ ≥ 0 and every such value is taken.
stages.solutionStepsEnglish: 1. Even exponent: x⁴ ≥ 0 and every such value is taken.

stages.headline: f(x) = x⁵. Compare f(−3) and f(−2).
stages.headlineEnglish: f(x) = x⁵. Compare f(−3) and f(−2).
stages.problemText: f(x) = x⁵. Compare f(−3) and f(−2).
stages.solutionSteps: 1. It is increasing. 2. −3 < −2, so f(−3) < f(−2).
stages.solutionStepsEnglish: 1. It is increasing. 2. −3 < −2, so f(−3) < f(−2).
